FINDING_ID: IM_F014
SEVERITY: 0.67
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `dynamic_management.py`, top docstring vs imports. The docstring states the immune review boundary is `_types.py + _immune.py + _manager.py`, but the same file places `FailureHandler` under the “Immune layer” import section and the user’s analytical boundary explicitly includes `FailureHandler`. This is not just a documentation typo: it misstates module ownership for an in-boundary component and can cause reviewers or tooling to omit `_failure_handler.py` from immune review. Evidence: docstring line “The immune layer review boundary is: _types.py + _immune.py + _manager.py.” versus actual import block `from bench.dm._failure_handler import FailureHandler, CorrelatedFailureModel`.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX: Replace the boundary sentence so it includes `_failure_handler.py`.

<<<<
The immune layer review boundary is: _types.py + _immune.py + _manager.py.
====
The immune layer review boundary is: _types.py + _immune.py + _failure_handler.py + _manager.py.
>>>>

FOLLOW: This fix requires the module inventory and any external review instructions to stay consistent with the corrected boundary. In particular, any reviewer guidance, test manifests, or decomposition docs derived from this docstring must be regenerated so `FailureHandler` is not silently excluded from immune review. VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F015
SEVERITY: 0.64
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `dynamic_management.py`, orchestrator re-export section. The shim’s own module inventory says `_manager.py` contains `DynamicManager (orchestrator, _REMEDIATION_CHAINS, apply_diagnosis, _apply_transform, process_round)`, but the actual import only re-exports `DynamicManager`. This breaks the stated backward-compatible contract for named immune-boundary call points. Evidence: inventory text names four additional `_manager.py` symbols; import is only `from bench.dm._manager import DynamicManager`.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX: Re-export the full `_manager.py` surface that the docstring claims is preserved.

<<<<
from bench.dm._manager import DynamicManager  # noqa: F401
====
from bench.dm._manager import (  # noqa: F401
    DynamicManager,
    _REMEDIATION_CHAINS,
    apply_diagnosis,
    _apply_transform,
    process_round,
)
>>>>

FOLLOW: This fix expands the shim’s public API. Any existing tests or consumers that introspect module members should be updated to include these symbols. It also reveals a downstream requirement: if `_manager.py` does not actually define module-level `apply_diagnosis`, `_apply_transform`, or `process_round` and they are instance methods instead, then the docstring is wrong and must be corrected instead of importing nonexistent names. VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F017
SEVERITY: 0.48
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.42
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `dynamic_management.py`, module structure inventory. `_manager.py` is described as containing `process_round`, but the shim does not make clear whether `process_round` is a module-level function or a `DynamicManager` method. In a compatibility shim, that distinction matters because consumers restoring old imports need to know whether `from dynamic_management import process_round` is valid. Evidence: inventory lists `_manager.py            DynamicManager (orchestrator, _REMEDIATION_CHAINS, apply_diagnosis, _apply_transform, process_round)` in a form that ambiguously mixes class contents and module-level symbols.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX: Rewrite the inventory entry to distinguish module-level exports from `DynamicManager` methods.

<<<<
    _manager.py            DynamicManager (orchestrator, _REMEDIATION_CHAINS,
                           apply_diagnosis, _apply_transform, process_round)
====
    _manager.py            DynamicManager orchestrator; plus compatibility
                           exports for _REMEDIATION_CHAINS, apply_diagnosis,
                           _apply_transform, and process_round if defined at
                           module scope
>>>>

FOLLOW: This fix exposes a downstream consistency requirement with IM_F015: either the shim must actually export these names, or the inventory must be narrowed to say they are methods on `DynamicManager` rather than module-level compatibility exports. One of those two representations must be chosen; keeping both ambiguous is incorrect. VERIFIED: TRUE
